summary: Intermittent top-k missing from rerank after embedding ingest with mixed protobuf charset and gzipped payloads
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent missing top-k results from rerank endpoint after bulk embedding uploads. Impact: ~5-10% of rerank requests return fewer than requested top-k items or return duplicates which the customer observes as missing unique hits. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east handling gzipped protobuf v2 payloads from the customer's ingestion pipeline. Observed after a recent client rollout that started sending protobuf with UTF-16LE string fields and gzip compression.

Observed behavior seems correlated with bursts of ingest (large batch uploads) and a specific combination: protobuf v2 + non-UTF8 string encoding + gzip. Hypothesis is that some embed IDs or metadata are mangled at proto decode step causing downstream shard routing to drop or de-dupe hits and trigger CPU fallback paths in reranker which increase latency and occasionally return truncated top-k lists.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Prepare a bulk embed payload encoded as protobuf v2 with string fields in UTF-16LE (customer client).
2) Gzip the payload and POST to /v1/embeddings/batch with content-encoding: gzip and content-type: application/x-protobuf;proto=embedded.v2
3) Wait for the embed-ingest ACK and then call /v1/rerank with the query referencing the same namespace and recent ids, requesting top_k=50
4) Observe in ~1 out of 10 runs that rerank returns fewer than 50 unique ids or contains duplicate ids with gaps in expected top_k ordering.

investigation_notes: 03/10 15:10 - Support (Aisha) validated with customer that the new client rollout started sending UTF-16LE string fields and enabled gzip on bulk uploads.

03/10 17:05 - Eng (Marcus) reproduced locally by constructing a gzipped proto v2 payload with UTF-16LE metadata; saw proto-transcoder warn about utf8_decode and subsequent checksum mismatch when pipeline attempted canonicalize metadata.

03/10 18:30 - Found code path in proto-transcoder that falls back to a best-effort conversion which can change byte-length of id or metadata used in sharding hash (we use metadata.title concatenated with id for shard key in this customer's namespace).

03/11 09:02 - Reranker team observed CPU-fallback sanitizer logic that collapses results when duplicate ids are detected and will reduce returned list length to avoid returning inconsistent scores. This is working as designed but is masking the underlying ingest corruption.
03/11 11:20 - SRE confirmed increased CPU across shard-17 during bursts, correlating with higher latency for rerank requests routed to cpu-fallback replicas.
comments: Aisha (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer noticed regressions after client upgrade; provided sample gzipped proto payload and example rerank request ids. Attached payload to ticket.

Marcus (Eng) 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally with synthetic payload. Proto-transcoder warns on non-UTF8 and we attempt best-effort decode which mutates the metadata string -> changes shard hash. Creating a focused test to verify id stability across transcode. Assigned to proto transport owners.

Elena (Reranker) 2026-03-11: Reranker sanitizer is catching duplicate ids and truncating list. This is correct behavior to avoid mis-scored outputs. However, we need upstream invariant that id+metadata used for routing is stable. Proposing temporary mitigation to accept canonicalized id metadata and de-dupe downstream while logging original id for audit.

Customer (NovusDocs) 2026-03-11: This behavior is impacting search result completeness in production. We cannot pause the client rollout; we can temporarily stop gzip or switch to UTF-8 encoding as a short-term workaround if helpful.

Marcus (Eng) 2026-03-12: Created PR to add stricter validation on proto-transcoder to reject non-UTF8 payloads with a clear error message instead of best-effort conversion: github.com/redwood-inference/proto-transcoder/pull/62. Also patch planned to preserve original id bytes for routing even when metadata conversion occurs.
root_cause: Proto-transcoder best-effort UTF-16LE -> UTF-8 conversion mutated metadata used in shard hashing, producing altered shard keys and duplicate ids observed by reranker sanitizer. The ingestion path did not reject or surface a hard error for non-UTF8 string encodings when gzip compression was present, leading to silent corruption during bursts.
workaround: Customer can (a) disable gzip on bulk ingestion, or (b) ensure client protobuf string fields are encoded in UTF-8. Both reduce the chance of proto-transcoder attempting best-effort conversion and will preserve sharding stability.
resolution: In progress - short-term: proto-transcoder PR added to reject non-UTF8 strings with 400 error and descriptive message (PR #62). Reranker team to add telemetry to surface duplicate-id-collapse events (instrumentation ticket created). Long-term: preserve original id bytes for routing and add a validation step in ingest to fail fast for unsupported encodings. Plan rollout: canary PR release to staging 03/13, prod rollout 03/15 after a 48h soak and customer opt-in.
follow_up_items: ENG: Merge proto-transcoder PR that returns 400 on non-UTF8 strings and add migration guidance to embed ingest docs.
SRE: Add alert for repeated 'duplicate-id-collapse' events per shard to #incidents and link to this ticket.
DOCS: Update embedding ingest best-practices page with explicit content-encoding and string encoding examples.
SUPPORT: Contact customer with step-by-step temporary workaround and confirm whether they will change client encoding or disable gzip.
